title: Insecure Randomness via Math.random for Tokens
platform_conditions: ECMAScript 2020 semantics; Math.random in V8 (Node.js and Chrome) is a 128-bit xorshift128+ PRNG whose state is recoverable from outputs
security_mechanism: Math.random is a pseudo-random generator seeded once per process and never reseeded; in V8 its xorshift128+ state can be reconstructed from a handful of observed outputs, after which all past and future outputs are predictable. Tokens, reset codes, and keys drawn from it are therefore guessable by anyone who can observe a few values (shares, leaderboards, timing endpoints) or read adjacent outputs. crypto.randomBytes / getRandomValues draw from the OS CSPRNG and do not share this weakness. Deprecated weak interfaces (md5 via createHash('md5') for credentials, single-DES) fail on the algorithm side the same way.

source_sink_clues.source: The token value itself: session identifiers, password-reset codes, API keys, CSRF nonces, and any secret the developer generated client-side or server-side with Math.random.
source_sink_clues.sink: Math.random() feeding token/key/nonce generation; crypto.createHash('md5'/'sha1') for credentials; deprecated weak cipher construction in crypto.createCipheriv

tracking_guards: Check security values come from crypto.randomBytes (Node) or crypto.getRandomValues (web), not Math.random; check credentials use a slow KDF or authenticated cipher from the crypto module; check comparers use crypto.timingSafeEqual.
not_candidate_when: Math.random drives only non-security behavior (animation, sampling, test fixtures, shuffling non-sensitive lists), the random value is combined with a CSPRNG source before use, or the fast hash digests content for integrity/dedup rather than authentication.
public_references: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/338.html
CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/327.html
